item.title: Chinese and US defense establishments maintain coordination on dialogues at different levels: Chinese defense ministry
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13 15:11:00
Chen Xi, spokesperson of China's Ministry of National Defense The Chinese and US militaries held the 4th Crisis Communication and Prevention Working Group meeting on November 2-3 in Washington, D.C.. The two sides had an in-depth exchange of views on how to deliver on the consensus reached by the two presidents, strengthen communication, and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation, Chen Xi, a spokesperson of the Ministry of National Defense said on Friday. Chen made the remarks when asked to provide further updates on China-US military-to-military engagement. According to a readout from the US Department of Defense, the US and Chinese militaries held a Crisis Communication and Prevention Working Group meeting in Washington, D.C.. Sources also indicate that the US Secretary of Defense and the Commander of the US Pacific Command might soon visit China. Chen said that building a stable, healthy and sustainable relationship between the Chinese and US militaries serves the shared interests of both sides and is a common expectation of the international community. The Chinese side values strategic communication with the US military, and the two defense establishments have maintained coordination on dialogues at different levels. We hope the US side will work with us to follow through on the important consensus reached by the two presidents, enhance communication, and properly manage differences, so as to add positive factors to building a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability, said Chen. Global Times

item.title: J-35A marks 2nd anniversary of its debut; state media analyzes upgrade prospects, including full version of WS-19 engine
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12 22:15:00
A full-scale model of the J-35A stealth fighter sits on display at the Dajiaochang Airport Runway Park in Nanjing, East China's Jiangsu Province, on November 10, 2026. Photo: VCG Thursday marked two years since the J-35A, China's domestically developed medium stealth multi-role fighter, made its public debut. As a new-generation stealth fighter, the J-35A has achieved key upgrades in avionics, situational awareness and weapons integration. State media CCTV News analyzed its upgrade prospects, mentioning an expected switch to using the full version of the domestically developed WS-19 turbofan engine. The J-35A, officially codenamed Yunlong (Cloud Dragon/Loong), is a single-seat, twin-engine fighter and the second type of fifth-generation stealth fighter jet independently developed by China, featuring the PLA Air Force's experience with and feedback on the J-20, China's first type of stealth fighter jet. The J-35A was designed with a balanced consideration of performance, reliability, maintainability and cost in mind, Wang Ya'nan, editor-in-chief of Beijing-based Aerospace Knowledge magazine, told the Global Times. For stealth, the J-35A uses an integrated low-observable design rather than relying on coatings alone. Its configuration features a blended wing body, twin canted vertical tails, all-moving horizontal tails and a diverterless supersonic inlet (DSI) to reduce radar reflections. Bay door seams follow edge-alignment principles, and integrated precision manufacturing reduces gap scattering. The cockpit canopy is coated with a conductive stealth film to compress radar returns, achieving multi-directional stealth, introduced CCTV. The radar cross section (RCS) of China's J-35 series is extremely small, thanks to its special fuselage design and China-exclusive metamaterial technologies, Wang noted. Such a small RCS allows the J-35 to remain undetected until it is very close to its target, giving it more advantages and opportunities in combat. This also means the J-35's stealth capability is at a world-class level. When it comes to avionics and situational awareness, the J-35A carries a new-generation active electronically scanned array radar, offering longer detection range and some capability against stealth targets. An electro-optical window under the nose provides electro-optical detection. The system supports sensor fusion and links with the pilot's helmet-mounted display, and can network with the J-20 and drones via high-speed data links, said CCTV. Military commentator Shao Yongling said in the CCTV News report that concerning weapons integration, the J-35A has an internal weapons bay for medium-range and short-range air-to-air missiles in stealth mode. The wings also have external hardpoints for air-to-ground and anti-ship munitions in non-stealth mode. With the public debut of the J-35A in November 2024, the Air Force's traditional "three swordsmen," the J-20 stealth fighter, J-16 fighter and J-10C fighter, have expanded and upgraded into a new "four swordsmen" lineup that includes two types of stealth fighters. The four "swordsmen" form a new combination in the Air Force's new-quality aviation combat power, CCTV reported. Shao noted that the J-20 is a high-end heavy fighter for high-value targets, while the J-35A is a medium fighter. They complement each other with clear differences in design and mission. The J-35A is smaller, cheaper and easier to maintain, making it better suited for large-scale fielding as a scalable, general-purpose stealth fighter. Its first core mission is routine air patrol and regional air defense. The second is multi-mission strikes: In stealth mode it can penetrate defenses and hit air defense sites, radars and ships; when needed, it switches to non-stealth mode with more munitions for air-to-ground and anti-ship support. It also supports system-based distributed operations, Shao said. China's J-35A fighter jet carries out its first adaptive training session at Zhuhai Jinwan Airport on November 8, 2024, ahead of the 15th China International Aviation and Aerospace Exhibition, also known as Airshow China, to be held in Zhuhai, South China's Guangdong Province. Photo: VCG In system confrontations, Shao said, once the J-20 opens a gap, large numbers of J-35As network with early warning aircraft and unmanned wingmen for wide-area surveillance and forward reconnaissance. Operating with fourth-generation fighters such as the J-16 and J-10C, the J-35A can slip in first to locate enemy radar and air defense sites and share coordinates with the rest of the formation, bringing stealth reconnaissance plus target guidance, the expert added. Despite these strengths, the CCTV report said the J-35A is far from the end point. From the start, it was designed with ample room for expansion of its capabilities. "A two-seat variant is technically feasible, and its core value would be as a command platform for unmanned wingmen. However, no official project has been announced. Besides a two-seat version, I think an electronic warfare variant is also an option," Shao was quoted by CCTV as saying. As for foreseeable upgrades to the J-35A, Shao sees four areas. First, the engine switching to the full version of the WS-19 turbofan engine. Second, Shao noted avionics and intelligence, which involves strengthening detection of stealth targets and reducing pilot workload through smarter systems. Third comes weapons and a bay expansion, which means optimizing the internal bay for more new munitions and a richer stealth-mode strike list. Finally, iterative stealth refinements will see improving stealth stability in complex environments. Overall, the J-35A is unlikely to pursue all-round upgrades at once, and will probably follow a "small-step, fast-iteration" path in batches, Shao said. Wang Yongqing, the chief designer of multiple types of aircraft as well as the chief expert of the Shenyang Aircraft Design and Research Institute under AVIC, previously described the J-35 series' development approach in an interview with Global Times. He said the J-35 series, developed with an "air-sea twin configuration" approach and a "one aircraft, multiple variants" concept, is expected to enter large-scale production in the future, with the aircraft acting as a "point guard" in systematic combat operations and delivering outstanding performance.

item.title: 77 years on, an ever-stronger PLA Air Force contributes to peace
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11 23:56:00
China's Bayi Aerobatic Team flies over Great Wall to mark Air Force's 77th anniversary Photo: Li Hao/Global Times Wednesday marked the 77th anniversary of the founding of the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) Air Force. After more than seven decades of development, the PLA Air Force has steadily advanced toward its strategic goal of "integrating air and space capabilities as well as coordinating offensive and defensive operations." With domestically developed new warplanes entering service as they are upgraded, the service has built an air combat force with a complete aircraft lineup, clear division of labor and efficient coordination, with modernization and system-based combat capability rising steadily. On Friday, six J-10 jets from the Chinese Air Force August 1st aerobatics team flew over the Great Wall as an anniversary tribute. On Monday, CCTV News' military channel released new footage offering a close-up, multi-angled look at the GJ-11 stealth drone, revealing its high-stealth characteristics, a buildup to the anniversary. Military affairs experts told the Global Times on Wednesday that in the new era, the Air Force's system-based combat capability has undergone profound changes and made great leaps. A series of broader international operations have also pushed domestic air power from "able to fly" toward "able to deploy far, coordinate across services and operate in unfamiliar environments." Building its force system for the future and accelerating modernization, the Air Force remains a defender of national sovereignty, security and development interests, and a steadfast guardian of peace and stability. System empowerment According to the CCTV News, looking back to the 1949 military parade marking the founding of the People's Republic of China, there were so few aircraft that they had to fly past twice to fill out the formation. After 77 years of hard work, the PLA Air Force started from that difficult position and gradually built a mature air and space combat system, completing a great strategic transition from homeland air defense to integrating air and space capabilities as well as coordinating offensive and defensive operations, Zhang Junshe, a Chinese military affairs expert, told the Global Times. In this transition, the main combat equipment system has continued to build and develop. With the public debut of the J-35A medium stealth multirole fighter, the Air Force's traditional "three swordsmen," the J-20 stealth fighter, J-16 fighter and J-10C fighter, have expanded and upgraded into a new "four swordsmen" lineup that includes two types of stealth fighters, CCTV reported. The four "swordsmen" form a new combination of the Air Force's aviation new-quality combat power, shaping a new air combat style of networked, coordinated air superiority and precision strikes across multiple aircraft types, CCTV reported. Zhang stressed that modern air combat is no longer a duel between single aircraft but a contest of systems. No matter how capable a single platform is, it can still create a weak link and struggle against complex, diverse battlefield threats. Deep integration and system empowerment across multiple services and aircraft types are essential, Zhang said. Fighters, bombers, early warning aircraft, tankers, electronic warfare aircraft, transport aircraft, reconnaissance drones and stealth drones each perform their roles and work closely together to build a solid air and space defense line, CCTV said. Beyond a complete equipment system, Zhang added, the Air Force's information hub is now stronger. Early warning aircraft serve as airborne command hubs, and data links act as the neural system, closely linking stealth fighters, drones, ground radar and air defense systems to achieve seamless connection between "seeing far" and "striking accurately." At the same time, new-quality combat forces are accelerating. High-stealth reconnaissance-strike drones operate alongside crewed fighters, pushing air and space confrontation into a new stage of intelligence and precision. The Air Force has all-domain offensive and defensive capability, not only with strong air superiority but also with breakthroughs in strategic early warning, long-range precision strikes, air and missile defense and strategic projection, achieving all-domain reach and combat capability, the expert said. CCTV reported that a modern strategic air force's combat power rests not only on advanced aviation equipment but on five core branches - aviation, ground-to-air missile, radar, airborne and electronic countermeasures - each performing its role in coordinated fashion, building a comprehensive, three-dimensional air and space defense system that is the core support for system-based air combat. An article from Outlook Weekly reposted by the Air Force's WeChat account said that at the upcoming 16th Airshow China in Zhuhai, Guangdong Province in December, the Air Force will maintain a system-based approach, coordinating static displays and flight performances to highlight iterative upgrades of main combat equipment. The share of new-quality combat forces will increase, and multiple main combat platforms will make their debuts. Exhibits will cover reconnaissance, early warning, air defense, support, airborne operations, unmanned applications, intelligent equipment and munitions, fully presenting the service's equipment renewal and evolving combat system. Growing global engagement On Wednesday, the PLA Air Force officially opened accounts on Facebook, YouTube, Instagram and X. The accounts will publish English short videos and posts on the Air Force's international exchanges, humanitarian operations and joint training, giving overseas audiences a more authentic, three-dimensional and comprehensive view of the PLA Air Force. Over the past year, the Air Force's external exchanges have widened and deepened. One of the highlights was that in August, the Air Force sent fighters, tankers, special mission aircraft and helicopters as a system to the China-Egypt Eagles of Civilization 2026 joint air training, focusing on air combat tactics, air superiority operations and combat search and rescue, along with force employment drills. During the training, PLA J-16s conducted air combat drills against Egyptian MiG-29 and Rafale fighters. A Chinese military affairs expert told the Global Times that the exercise marked China's first deployment of the J-16 and Egypt's first participation by Rafale fighters, reflecting a relatively high level of mutual trust and a considerable standard of joint training. Zhang said international joint training sessions enable the PLA Air Force to further turn equipment advantages into system capabilities, pushing domestic air power from "able to fly" toward "able to deploy far, coordinate across services and operate in unfamiliar environments." It tested and improved long-range projection and support, and honed system-based combat tactics and capabilities. It accumulated operational experience in foreign environments and drove continuous tactical upgrading, and spurred industrial development. Overseas users' operating habits, maintenance conditions and mission needs feed back into modular design, logistic supply and lifecycle support, ultimately benefiting domestic fielding, Zhang said. Beyond joint training, the PLA Air Force serves as an emissary of China's image and responsibility as a major power, observers noted. In September, an Air Force Y-20 transport aircraft carried multiple batches of relief supplies to Nepal for emergency humanitarian aid after mudslide disasters. In February, the August 1st Aerobatic Team performed in Singapore, its first public appearance there after switching to the J-10C. The complex and spectacular performance won wide praise. Song Zhongping, a Chinese military affairs expert, told the Global Times that an air force is a concentrated expression of a country's military and industrial capability. Along with the Air Force's growing strength, Chinese-made fighters are gaining global recognition and broad export prospects. This year, Uzbekistan's official media reported that the country had procured the J-10CE from China. Beyond that, countries including Bangladesh and Indonesia are reportedly advancing procurement or showing interest in the fighter. Song said that while the use of Chinese aviation equipment continues to increase in foreign trade cooperation, China's arms exports only contribute to regional peace and stability and help countries improve their foundational capacity for self-defense, just as the Air Force's modernization serves to safeguard national sovereignty, security and development interests and defend peace and stability. Committed to being a builder of world peace, a contributor to global development and a defender of the international order, the Chinese Air Force's flight paths across the world contribute important strength to safeguarding world peace and promoting win-win cooperation, Outlook Weekly said. "From trailing behind to running neck and neck, the PLA Air Force has traveled an extraordinary path. As China's technological and economic strength continues to grow, the Air Force and aviation industry are expected to develop further and rapidly, bringing greater miracles and more opportunities in the good for world peace," Song said.

item.title: China develops drone capable of injecting emergency medication into wounded personnel from a distance
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11 21:23:00
Photo: CCTV China's Air Force Medical University has developed what it describes as the military's first casualty-search drone and made progress in using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to administer emergency medication to wounded personnel from a distance, state broadcaster CCTV reported Wednesday. "We have developed the military's first casualty-search drone, and have also made some breakthroughs in treatment. For example, we can use drones to inject medication into wounded personnel from a considerable distance," Wang Jianqi, a representative of Air Force Medical University, was quoted as saying in the report. "Wherever our drone can fly, we can deliver life-saving emergency medication into a wounded person's muscle, buying valuable time for treatment," he said. The development comes as unmanned equipment is being adapted to a broader range of battlefield medical tasks, including locating casualties, delivering medical supplies and potentially transporting wounded personnel to field hospitals or designated medical facilities. Military commentator Song Zhongping told the Global Times on Wednesday that the changing nature of modern warfare has made battlefield medical rescue increasingly challenging, as the distinction between the front lines and the rear has become less clear. "One of the biggest problems in modern warfare is that it has blurred the concept of the front lines and the rear. The two have even merged into one, meaning that the areas where casualties may occur have become extremely extensive," Song told the Global Times. He cited the Russia-Ukraine conflict and conflicts in the Middle East as examples, saying attacks can take place in areas far beyond what would traditionally be considered the front lines, making the distribution of casualties less predictable. Against this backdrop, drones can help deliver medication and medical supplies to wounded personnel in areas that are difficult or dangerous for rescue teams to reach in time, Song said. "The drone-based injection of medication is essentially an extension of using drones to deliver medicine. It helps ensure that wounded personnel on the battlefield receive initial treatment," he said. In the video, a UAV can be seen releasing a dart toward a soldier lying on the ground. In traditional battlefield rescue operations, medical personnel often have to expose themselves to considerable danger to reach wounded personnel. The use of unmanned equipment could reduce the need for medical teams to enter high-risk areas, while also helping stabilize casualties before evacuation, Song said. "Some wounded personnel at the front lines need pain relief before they can be moved back," Song said. "If drones and other unmanned equipment are used to transport them, it is also necessary to stabilize their condition in advance, so that no secondary danger arises during transportation." He added that the approach could also be useful in civilian emergency response, particularly in areas affected by landslides, collapsed roads or rivers that prevent rescue teams from reaching people in need. "Using drones to transport people or deliver medication into such areas is a relatively good approach," Song said, adding that unmanned equipment could help address urgent rescue needs without exposing helicopters and their crews to the same level of risk. However, the development of unmanned medical rescue still faces technical challenges. According to Wang, air-ground unmanned treatment remains at an exploratory stage, with researchers still working to overcome key technological difficulties, including how to retrieve and load wounded personnel onto drones for evacuation. Other Chinese military medical units have also been exploring the use of unmanned systems in battlefield rescue training. In a drill organized by the PLA Joint Logistic Support Force's 967th Hospital, a thermal-imaging drone was used to locate simulated casualties, while smaller cargo drones and robotic dogs delivered emergency medical supplies to areas inaccessible to conventional rescue vehicles, the PLA Daily reported in October. Robotic dogs were also used to enter narrow passages and transmit information about casualties and surrounding conditions, according to the report.

item.title: China trains peacekeepers from developing countries in drone ops
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-10 21:07:00
Chinese UN peacekeepers march through Tian'anmen Square during a military parade in Beijing, on September 3, 2025. Photo: VCG China has stepped up efforts to help developing countries strengthen their capabilities in UN peacekeeping operations, with a peacekeeping drone training course concluding in Xi'an, Northwest China's Shaanxi Province, a front-page report by the PLA Daily said Tuesday. The three-week program was jointly organized by the Ministry of National Defense's Peacekeeping Affairs Center and the Air Force Engineering University, and brought together trainees from China, the UN and eight countries including Algeria, Malaysia and South Africa. The course comes as drones are playing an increasingly prominent role in military operations and other security-related activities, presenting new challenges for UN peacekeeping forces, military commentator Song Zhongping told the Global Times. "If both sides involved in a conflict possess drone capabilities, but UN peacekeeping forces do not have the corresponding capabilities, they will be unable to effectively carry out their peacekeeping mandate," Song told the Global Times, adding that drone operation and counter-drone technologies have increasingly become essential skills for peacekeepers. According to the PLA Daily report, the training covered 31 topics, including the principles governing the use of drones in UN peacekeeping operations, deployment, command and control, safety management and logistical support. Experts delivered theoretical lectures, while trainees also participated in comprehensive exercises based on conflict mediation scenarios in UN mission areas. At the request of the UN, the course included a counter-drone technology and application module for the first time. It also increased the proportion of practical training to better prepare participants for operational responsibilities. Song said developing countries contribute a substantial share of UN peacekeeping personnel, but their military capabilities, including their ability to operate and counter drones, may be comparatively limited. "China has extensive experience in both the use of drones and counter-drone operations," he said. "Sharing such experience with other countries, and potentially providing relevant equipment in the future, could help improve the effectiveness of UN peacekeeping operations." The importance of strengthening counter-drone capabilities has also been recognized in the UN's own discussions on peacekeeping. A 2026 report of the UN Special Committee on Peacekeeping Operations encouraged the UN Secretariat and member states to strengthen the exchange of expertise and training cooperation on counter-unmanned aircraft systems, and to work toward developing a framework for counter-drone systems in UN peacekeeping operations. China has increasingly expanded its international peacekeeping training to cover both traditional areas and emerging technological requirements. In addition to courses for military observers, staff officers and peacekeeping instructors, Chinese military institutions have introduced specialized programs on drone operation and comprehensive situational awareness, according to the report. Since 2015, the Ministry of National Defense's Peacekeeping Affairs Center has organized more than 30 international peacekeeping training courses and dispatched multiple groups of experts to provide overseas instruction, training peacekeeping Song said China's participation in such training reflects its responsibilities as a permanent member of the UN Security Council and its commitment to supporting the UN peacekeeping system. "Peacekeeping missions are facing increasingly complex and demanding challenges, while the equipment and experience of peacekeeping forces have not always kept pace with the situations they encounter," he said. "Strengthening their capabilities is therefore essential to ensuring that peacekeepers can better fulfill their mandates and protect personnel in the field." China, as a major country in drone technology and equipment, is in a position to share its experience and technical expertise with other troop-contributing countries, Song noted.

item.title: State media new footage offers rare, multi-angle look at GJ-11 drone, revealing design details behind its stealth
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-09 21:24:00
The GJ-11 stealth drone Photo: Screenshot from CCTV News military channel CCTV News military channel released new footage on Monday offering a close-up, multi-angle look at the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) Air Force's GJ-11 stealth drone. It also revealed that two of the Air Force's first batch of self-trained female drone operators scored a first-round hit during the GJ-11's first live-fire strike mission. A military affairs expert explained how the design features shown in the video contribute to its stealth performance, and said the model has likely achieved combat and support capability, with technical maturity sufficiently assured. The GJ-11, codenamed "Xuanlong," is a domestically developed tailless flying-wing drone. The footage showed the GJ-11 up close, with details including its air intake, exhaust nozzle, landing gear and internal weapons bay doors revealing its high-stealth characteristics. According to CCTV, the GJ-11 has an air intake on top of its fuselage, a flattened tail section, and all weapons carried internally in a belly weapons bay that can accommodate a variety of air-to-surface munitions. It offers strong stealth, long endurance and high strike accuracy, and can carry out missions including air strikes and suppression of enemy air defense (SEAD). Song Zhongping, a Chinese military affairs expert, told the Global Times on Monday that the multi-angle display makes the GJ-11's distinctive stealth design clearer. Its dorsal air intake is a design that enhances stealth, and its exhaust nozzle has also been treated for stealth, further improving survivability and enabling stealth-based penetration. It also uses radar-absorbing coatings to further reduce its radar cross-section. The CCTV military channel also revealed on Monday that two post-95s drone operators Shi Xiaoran and Fu Ting are among the first batch of female drone operators trained independently by the PLA Air Force. From newcomers to skilled operators, they completed their conversion training in just five months. In the GJ-11's first live-fire strike mission, Shi and Fu worked closely with their comrades and scored a first-round hit. A close-up look at the landing gear and internal weapons bay doors of the GJ-11 stealth drone Photo: Screenshot from CCTV News military channel CCTV said that the GJ-11 is a pioneer and a pathfinder. In future operations, striking ground targets will be a high-risk mission, and unmanned attack aircraft can reduce losses of personnel and weapons platforms. It will become an important partner and the most effective loyal wingman for main combat aircraft. Drone operators control the entire flight from inside a command cabin, issuing various instructions to manage the aircraft's attitude amid rapidly changing conditions. Their combat-oriented training in the cabin, tailored to mission needs, typically runs more than six hours per session, sometimes counted in days. The cabin is designed for mobile deployment: if a mission requires it, the entire cabin can be loaded directly onto a transport aircraft and sent straight to the front line, reported CCTV. "I found that drone iteration is beyond imagination. Many scenarios that appeared in sci-fi films are already being tried in real-world applications. In future battlefields, what matters more is a smart brain's perception of the battlefield situation and precise control of equipment. None of this has anything to do with gender, only with proficiency and hours of operation," Shi was quoted by CCTV as saying. The GJ-11 stealth attack drone was first unveiled at China's National Day military parade held in Beijing in 2019. It later made its appearance at China International Aviation and Aerospace Exhibition (also known as Airshow China) in Zhuhai, South China's Guangdong Province, in 2021. On this occasion, the GJ-11 opened its two belly weapons bays, each holding several precision-guided bombs, Global Times reporters observed at the scene. In November 2025, the PLA Air Force released a short film marking its 76th anniversary, revealing that the GJ-11 had entered service. The appearance marked the Air Force's official entry into a new model of manned-unmanned cooperative operations, said CCTV. The short film also showed for the first time an aerial formation composed of the GJ-11 stealth drone, the J-20 stealth fighter and the J-16D electronic warfare aircraft. Song called it a perfect combination for breaking through enemy defenses. A close-up look at the exhaust nozzle of the GJ-11 stealth drone Photo: Screenshot from CCTV News military channel Song supposed that the GJ-11 had undergone extensive testing before being fielded and forming aerial formations with the J-20 and J-16D, all core tests of its performance. He noted that the GJ-21, recently showcased alongside the Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan, is in fact a carrier-based variant improved on the GJ-11. The GJ-11, as its predecessor, has likely achieved combat and support capability with sufficient technical maturity. The shift from an Air Force model to a Navy variant also shows the Air Force version's technical foundation is already mature, the expert said. With the 16th Airshow China approaching, military commentator Zhang Xuefeng said this year's show is expected to feature new drones. Whether the GJ-11 will appear and whether it can perform formation flights with other fighters are both worth watching. The GJ-11 is not the only advanced drone China has developed. At the V-Day military parade in Beijing on September 3, 2025, China for the first time displayed multiple types of wingman drones and air superiority drones. Military affairs experts told the Global Times that some of the UAVs showcased at the parade not only have new appearances, but also embody new concepts, which could overturn the existing air combat scenarios and profoundly change the future of air combat.

item.title: PLA Navy's first female shipborne pilots pass graduation assessment, to join aircraft carrier fleet
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-08 15:31:00
One of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Navy's first-batch female shipborne flight cadets operates a carrier-based helicopter. Photo: Screenshot from PLA Navy WeChat account The Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) Navy's first batch of female shipborne pilot trainees have all passed their graduation assessments and reported to frontline units, marking a new addition to the PLA Navy's aviation talent pool and a breakthrough in shipborne pilot training, state media outlets reported on Saturday. A military affairs expert noted that the first batch of female shipborne pilots now on duty fly helicopters, and that as the training system continues to mature, more female pilots, including female fixed-wing carrier fighter pilots, are expected in the future. "Take off!" At around 9 am, following tower instructions, trainee pilot Han Meng lifted her aircraft smoothly into the air, completing hovering, takeoff acceleration, instrument flight and platform landing in succession, a smooth, precise sequence that carried her through the assessment, the PLA Navy reported. These pilots had previously passed demanding assessments, including day and night landings, confined-area takeoffs and landings, and search and rescue. This graduation assessment focused on crew resource management and overall flight proficiency, testing their precision and mental resilience through every steady hover, instrument pass and every platform landing, the PLA Navy said. Recruited in 2023 as fresh graduates of military and civilian universities, they are the PLA Navy's first batch of female pilot trainees, all born after 2000 and trained by the Naval Aviation University. The first female shipborne pilot trainees underwent rigorous selection, live-aircraft screening, enlistment training, aviation theory study and aircraft type conversion, then completed the full flight training syllabus and passing their graduation assessments, according to the Xinhua News Agency. In recent years, as Chinese naval aviation has shifted from shore-based to shipborne operations, recruitment scope, selection methods and training models for shipborne pilot trainees have been continuously expanded and optimized. The Naval Aviation University has moved difficult subjects once taught only in combat units into the academy phase, greatly shortening the growth cycle for flight personnel and accelerating combat capability generation, Xinhua said. "Passing the graduation assessment is not the end, but a new starting point," Han was quoted by the PLA Navy WeChat account as saying. After joining frontline posts, they will keep pushing forward, study hard and train rigorously, ready at any time to be tested by real missions. According to Xinhua, the trainees will deploy aboard aircraft carriers and other large and medium-sized surface vessels for diversified missions. Wang Yunfei, a Chinese military affairs expert, told the Global Times on Sunday that they are the first group of female shipborne pilots in the history of the Chinese Navy, marking a historic breakthrough in shipborne flight personnel development and filling a long-standing gap in female naval pilot roles. With the three-carrier system taking shape, demand for pilots keeps growing, Wang said. He noted that for a long time, shipborne flight posts in China were almost entirely held by male pilots. But modern naval warfare is no longer about raw physical strength; it is about precision control, electronic analysis and data interpretation. Regardless of gender, shipborne pilots are the best of the best. The recruitment of female shipborne pilots will optimize the talent structure and expand the reserve, and the new talent mix can complement strengths, improve rotation, shift and long-voyage systems, and make carrier group combat duty more sustained and efficient, Wang said. Globally, the expert said, training female shipborne pilots is already standard among leading naval powers. The experiences of the US, France and the UK all show that women are fully capable of high-intensity shipborne flight and are an important part of naval combat power. Notably, footage from the PLA Navy report shows these shipborne pilots flying shipborne helicopters. Wang explained that training shipborne helicopter pilots lays a foundation for training female fixed-wing pilots by providing extensive experience in shipborne takeoffs and landings, adaption to maritime conditions and personnel training. Since female shipborne helicopter pilots are now formally on duty, as training models improve and systems mature, female fixed-wing carrier fighter pilots are also expected in the future, a trend of the times, Wang added. In August, this first batch of female shipborne pilot trainees all passed their daytime shipborne landing qualification assessments and entered the night landing training and evaluation phase, drawing coverage from multiple media outlets. Shipborne landing is a critical milestone in a shipborne pilot's development, often described as the "certificate" for entry into real naval aviation. Passing assessment marks a significant step in the PLA Navy's efforts to cultivate female shipborne aviation talent, according to CCTV News on August 14.

item.title: Experts highlight role of automated assistance system in GJ-21 stealth drone's takeoff and landing aboard Type 076 amphibious assault ship
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-07 21:11:00
A simulated animation of a GJ-21 armed reconnaissance stealth drone on board a Type 076 amphibious assault ship. Photo: Screenshot from CCTV News China's first amphibious assault ship equipped with electromagnetic catapults, the Type 076 Sichuan , has made further progress in recent days, with the GJ-21 stealth drone completing its first takeoff and landing operations aboard the vessel. An expert highlighted the significance of automated assistance systems in a report released on Saturday. Another expert noted that, with its unmanned design, the GJ-21 faces no human physical limitations during takeoff and landing and could potentially be adapted for use not only on the Type 076 amphibious assault ship but also on aircraft carriers in the future, including conventionally powered ones. The GJ-21 stealth unmanned aerial vehicle features a tailless flying-wing design with a blended wing-body configuration. It is equipped with an internal weapons bay and internal fuel storage, according to CCTV News. The platform designed to operate it, the Sichuan , is the first hull of the Type 076 amphibious assault ship, which is designed, developed and built independently by China. It has a full-load displacement of more than 40,000 tons. Wei Dongxu, a Chinese military affairs commentator, said that the carrier-based aircraft landings are technically challenging because an aircraft carrier itself is moving at sea. Pilots must constantly adjust the aircraft's altitude, flight angle and speed, while ensuring that its tailhook catches an arresting cable on the carrier's flight deck, according to CCTV News. However, the GJ-21 is uncrewed and operates as an intelligent combat platform. Therefore, it is highly likely that the GJ-21 and the Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan will rely on intelligent and automated assistance systems, Wei added. "For example, through signals, the GJ-21 could autonomously sense the Sichuan's navigation conditions to a certain extent, adjust itself and adapt accordingly, ultimately completing the entire landing sequence efficiently, quickly and precisely," Wei continued, CCTV reported. As the aircraft is unmanned, there is no need to account for the physical stress that pilots would experience during takeoff and landing, Wang Yunfei, a Chinese military affairs expert, told the Global Times. Compared with manned aircraft of a smaller size and weight, it can take off and land more quickly, with less stringent requirements for climb and descent angles, and conduct more sorties, he added. On the other hand, Wang noted that UAVs place higher demands on flight control and command systems. During takeoff and landing, they may encounter wind updrafts or downdrafts. Unlike manned aircraft, where pilots can make immediate adjustments, UAVs rely heavily on onboard AI and remote-control systems. The successful takeoff and landing of the GJ-21 on board the Type 076 amphibious assault ship showed that China has reached the world's highest level in terms of drone adaptability on aircraft carrier. Wang also noted that aircraft carriers by conventional means could also adopt this automated takeoff and landing assistance system in the future. "If it works successfully on the Type 076 amphibious assault ship, it should theoretically be possible to adapt it for other aircraft carriers," he said. Once the system has been tested on the Sichuan and sufficient test data has been collected, it could potentially be introduced on other carriers equipped with electromagnetic catapults, he added. "This would expand the range of aircraft operating from our carriers and further enhance their unmanned combat capabilities."

item.title: Successful takeoff & landing of China's GJ-21 shipborne stealth drone marks milestone for new combat capabilities; China pursues defensive defense policy: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06 15:54:00
Chen Xi, spokesperson of China's Ministry of National Defense The successful first takeoff and landing of the GJ-21 stealth drone on the amphibious assault ship Sichuan marks an important milestone in developing the PLA's new-domain and new-quality combat capabilities, Chen Xi, a spokesperson of the Ministry of National Defense, said on Friday, stressing that China pursues peaceful development and consistently follows a defensive national defense policy. Chen made the remarks when asked to comment on reports which claimed China's first carrier-based stealth strike and reconnaissance drone has completed takeoff and landing trials aboard the Sichuan. Some media argue this will extend the PLA Navy's long-range operational reach and shift the maritime power balance in the Western Pacific. Guided by operational requirements and keeping pace with global military technological advances, we are accelerating the modernization of weaponry and equipment — purely to safeguard national sovereignty, security and development interests, Chen said. China remains a force for peace, stability and progress in the world, Chen added. Global Times
